label: D1 dip after reaching S2 (esp. rewarded), growing sharply over last ~10 episode trials
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5) ;; (phase == D1) * prev_reward * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * prev_reward * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/5)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 39 sits near 1 (mean 0.987); GO and D2 are almost flat. Its variance is the D1 step, where it drops, and the drop gets much bigger near the end of the episode (timing alone gives R^2 0.58). Beyond timing, the D1 value is set by the previous trial outcome, and that effect is multiplied by a sharp late-episode weight exp((ep_trial-99)/5). Reaching S2 on the last trial lowers z (weight -0.12 x late weight), and a rewarded S2 lowers it most (another -0.18; a2 S2 r / a1 S2 r at trials 95-99 fall to about 0.6-0.75). At D1, a reached S1 raises it slightly at any time (+0.016). Reaching S2 via the rare a1 transition lowers it a bit more (-0.04). A rewarded trial two back, and a1 as the last choice, raise it a little late in the episode. The ideal-observer belief log-odds add a small graded term late in the episode. GO/D2 belief effects (about 0.001) are negligible. Uses observed quantities only, no future variables. Dev R^2 beyond timing is 0.59 and test is 0.57. That beats the profile additive all ceiling of 0.41 (all observed 0.39) because the terms interact with episode time. The earlier model-output explanation was not rerun here, but policy decile alone gave only 0.12 in the reference scores, so observed-only loses little. Remaining misses: a1 S2 r at D1 is over-predicted, and there is some streak dependence across several S2-rewarded trials.

issues: Upheld. The claimed terms reproduce test R^2 beyond timing of 0.567. The weights match the explanation: S2 x late -0.12, S2 x reward x late -0.18, constant S1 +0.016, constant rare a1->S2 -0.037, belief_lo x late -0.017, reward two trials back x late +0.042.

Each claim holds up when its term is changed or removed (test split). Dropping the constant S1 term gives 0.49. Making the S1 term late-weighted gives 0.51, and limiting it to before trial 60 gives 0.51, so 'at any point in the episode' is right. The core S2 / S2-rewarded late terms on their own give 0.26. Changing the exp time constant to 3 or 10 trials gives 0.55-0.56, so the exact shape matters little.

The explanation undersells the rare a1->S2 term. It is a constant over the whole episode, not late-weighted, and removing it drops test R^2 from 0.567 to 0.45. 'Lowers it a little more' understates that. The profile residuals agree: after a1 S2 u the D1 residual is -0.036, versus -0.005 after a2 S2 u.

Missing error class: the worst-fit windows are dominated by D1 on the window's first trial, where prev_state = -1 is unknown. Typical cases: actual 0.62-0.69 vs predicted 0.92-0.96 (e.g. [-3 t95] r1 0.628/0.928). The previous trial lies outside the window, so the S2 terms cannot fire. A belief-based proxy, prev_state==-1 x prev_reward x (belief_lo<0) x late, gets weight -0.29 but closes these misses only partly. This is a window-edge limitation and the explanation does not mention it.

The remaining systematic errors are small and mostly the ones the explanation already names. D1 after a1 S2 r is over-predicted by -0.015. D1 after unrewarded trials is under-predicted by about +0.006. Rewarded S2 streaks are real: the term S2r x S2r-two-back x late gets weight +0.04 and raises test R^2 to 0.583, so this is a small effect.

The claim that the fit beats the additive ceiling (0.41) holds on test (0.567) because the terms interact with episode time. The loss from leaving out model outputs was not checked directly. It is inferred from the policy-decile reference score of 0.12.
